name: Moraine Lake
what: Glacier-fed lake in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, reached from Lake Louise by Parks Canada shuttle or commercial tour only.
why_must_do: Most photographed lake in the Rockies; Rockpile viewpoint and canoes.
booking_needed: Yes: Parks Canada shuttle (2026: opened 15 Apr 2026 8am MT, 40% of seats, rest released 48h ahead; ran 1 Jun-12 Oct 2026; adult 12.75, youth 4.00, +3.50 online fee). Private vehicles not allowed on Moraine Lake Road year-round.
child_note: Flat lakeshore (1.3 km one way) and Rockpile (0.7 km loop) suit a 6 year old. Shuttle fare tiers for youth: GAP age bands not verified.

name: Lake Louise
what: Turquoise glacial lake below Victoria Glacier with a flat lakeshore trail.
why_must_do: Iconic Rockies lake; lakeshore walk and Fairview Lookout.
booking_needed: Parking at lake is pay/limited; Lakeshore shuttle ran 15 May-12 Oct 2026 via Park and Ride (reserve)
child_note: Lakeshore trail 2.3 km one way is easy; stroller-capable surface not verified (GAP).

name: Johnston Canyon
what: Catwalk trail through a limestone canyon to Lower and Upper Falls.
why_must_do: Easy catwalk walk with waterfalls; Ink Pots beyond.
child_note: Lower Falls 1.1 km one way, 85 m: fine for a 6 year old; exposed catwalks, hold hands. 2026 pattern: Johnston Canyon Trail closed from 13 Oct 2026 for rock slope work, status for Sept 2029 is GAP.

name: Peyto Lake Lookout
what: Viewpoint over a bright blue wolf-head-shaped lake from Bow Summit.
why_must_do: Best easy view on the Icefields Parkway.
best_time: Morning, light is best before noon
child_note: 0.6 km one way, 30 m gain; paved to lookout is GAP (not verified).

name: Bow Lake
what: Large lake on the Icefields Parkway below Crowfoot Glacier, trailhead for Bow Glacier Falls.
why_must_do: Roadside lake, picnic, Num-Ti-Jah Lodge.
child_note: Bow Glacier Falls trail 3.8 km one way, 95 m (too long for the little one, lakeside strolling is fine).

name: Vermilion Lakes Drive
what: Scenic drive and wetland lakes on the edge of Banff townsite facing Mount Rundle.
why_must_do: Sunrise/sunset views and elk and bird watching.
child_note: Short stops, flat. GAP: no official page fetched for this sight; description is general knowledge.

name: Cave and Basin National Historic Site
what: Birthplace of Canada's national park system with a warm mineral spring cave.
why_must_do: History plus boardwalk walks to marsh.
child_note: Good rainy-day child stop. GAP: no official page fetched for this sight; description is general knowledge.

name: Banff Gondola (Sulphur Mountain)
what: Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain with boardwalk and viewing deck.
why_must_do: Big views with almost no walking; replaces the 4.8 km one-way, 655 m Sulphur Mountain trail.
booking_needed: Private operator, book ahead in Sept long weekend; GAP: price/hours not verified
child_note: Height requirements: GAP. Private operator, not Parks Canada.

name: Lake Minnewanka
what: Largest lake in Banff National Park with a short Stewart Canyon trail and cruise.
why_must_do: Easy lake walk, scenic cruise.
child_note: Lake Minnewanka Trail to Stewart Canyon bridge is 1.6 km one way, 30 m. 2026: trail past Stewart Canyon bridge, Aylmer Pass and several campgrounds closed from 16 Sep until further notice; Aylmer trails have group restriction 10 Jul-15 Sep.

name: Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93N) scenic drive
what: 230 km scenic drive between Lake Louise and Jasper through the Banff and Jasper icefields.
why_must_do: Spine of the trip, with Peyto, Bow Lake, Columbia Icefield, Athabasca and Sunwapta Falls.
best_time: Early morning start, Sept snow possible at Bow Summit
child_note: Long drive for a 6 year old, plan frequent stops. Gas stations limited: GAP not verified.

name: Athabasca Glacier and Columbia Icefield
what: Toe of the Athabasca Glacier and the Columbia Icefield, roadside viewing with a walk to the glacier toe.
why_must_do: Walk to the toe of a glacier you can see from the road.
booking_needed: Glacier Adventure tours are private operator, book ahead: GAP not verified
child_note: Toe trail 1.8 km round trip, 60 m: feasible. Do not walk on the ice. Icefield Centre information desk closed per 2026 page.

name: Sunwapta Falls
what: Powerful waterfall on the Sunwapta River just off the Icefields Parkway.
why_must_do: Easy roadside falls.
child_note: Upper falls viewpoint is short and fenced; Lower Sunwapta Falls trail 2.6 km round trip, 87 m. Trailhead and picnic site open per 2026 page.

name: Athabasca Falls
what: Powerful falls and canyon on the Athabasca River.
why_must_do: Very short walk, big water.
child_note: 200 m walk, fenced viewpoints; hold hands near canyon edges. Day-use area open per 2026 page.

name: Maligne Lake and Spirit Island
what: Largest lake in Jasper, boat cruise to Spirit Island.
why_must_do: One of the most photographed spots in the Rockies.
best_time: Morning; Sept cruises run until end of season GAP
booking_needed: Cruise is private operator, book ahead: GAP not verified
child_note: Cruise requires little walking; life jackets for child supplied by operator: GAP. Maligne Road reopened 11 Oct 2024; trailhead, boathouse picnic site open per 2026 page; Spirit Island cruise not confirmed on the page.

name: Maligne Canyon
what: Deep limestone canyon with waterfalls and bridges near Jasper.
why_must_do: Normally a top family walk.
child_note: CLOSED 2026: Superintendent closure, no public access (2026-10-08 trail conditions) and 'closed until further notice' on the Across the River page. Status in Sept 2029 is GAP.

name: Pyramid Lake
what: Lake and island with the iconic Pyramid Mountain backdrop near Jasper townsite.
why_must_do: Easy sunset spot, picnic, boat rental.
child_note: Pyramid Bench trails reopened per 2026 page; trailhead open. Lake Annette Loop (2.4 km flat) is nearby.

name: Jasper Townsite
what: Mountain town and park base, rebuilt after the July 2024 wildfire.
why_must_do: Town services, dining, base for Maligne and Icefields.
booking_needed: Accommodation: book early for Sept long weekend
child_note: Town stroll. Post-wildfire burn area safety guidance: see Parks Canada page.

name: Miette Hot Springs
what: Hot springs pools at the end of Miette Road east of Jasper.
why_must_do: Soak after hiking; Sulphur Skyline trail nearby.
child_note: Miette Hot Springs open per 2026 page. Water temperature for a 6 year old: GAP.

name: Mount Edith Cavell and Cavell Meadows
what: Cavell Road to Angel Glacier viewpoint and the Path of the Glacier.
why_must_do: Glacier views.
child_note: CLOSED 2026: Cavell Road and day-use area closed; trails 41 Path of the Glacier and 42 Cavell Meadows closed (debris flow risk). Sept 2029 status GAP.

name: Emerald Lake
what: Emerald-green lake with a flat 5.2 km shoreline loop and lodge.
why_must_do: Easy flat loop, canoe rental.
child_note: Emerald Lakeshore 5.2 km loop, minimal gain, muddy and rooty on east side.

name: Takakkaw Falls
what: 373 m waterfall at the end of Yoho Valley Road.
why_must_do: Tallest falls on the trip, flat paved walk to base.
best_time: Road open mid-June to mid-October; late-day cloud
child_note: 0.9 km one way flat paved path. Yoho Valley Road switchbacks: trailers not allowed GAP.

name: Natural Bridge
what: Rock bridge carved by the Kicking Horse River, near the Emerald Lake road turnoff.
why_must_do: Roadside quick stop.
child_note: Almost no walking. Parking is about 4 km west of Field on Emerald Lake Road. Distance to bridge: GAP.

name: Wapta Falls
what: Broad 30 m waterfall on the Kicking Horse River.
why_must_do: Easy forest walk to a large falls.
best_time: Anytime; road closed late Oct to late May
child_note: 2.2 km one way, 80 m gain: family-friendly per Parks Canada. Eastbound access only from the highway.

name: Marble Canyon
what: Narrow marble canyon with bridges and a rim walk.
why_must_do: Short, easy, high impact.
child_note: 0.9 km one way, 65 m. Fenced bridges.

name: Paint Pots
what: Three iron-rich mineral springs staining ochre ground.
why_must_do: Easy flat walk; Indigenous cultural site.
child_note: 1 km one way, 35 m. Good for 6 year old.

name: Radium Hot Springs
what: Hot mineral pools at the park's west gate in Sinclair Canyon.
why_must_do: Soak and swim break.
child_note: Pool depth/age rules: GAP. 2026 note: Hot Springs trail connector to Sinclair Canyon closed for road construction.

name: Waterton Townsite
what: Lakeside village in Waterton Lakes National Park with shoreline cruise and Bear's Hump trail.
why_must_do: Compact base; wildlife and prairie-meets-mountain scenery.
child_note: Town shoreline paths flat. Wildlife corridor caution on Entrance Road per 2026 notice.

name: Red Rock Parkway and Red Rock Canyon
what: 15 km scenic drive to Red Rock Canyon with a short loop and Blakiston Falls.
why_must_do: Easy red argillite canyon walk.
best_time: Open until October; closed to motor vehicles Oct-May
child_note: Red Rock Canyon Loop open per 2026 page. Loop length: GAP, INFERENCE 0.7 km.

name: Cameron Lake
what: Subalpine lake at the end of Akamina Parkway on the Continental Divide.
why_must_do: Boat rental, grizzly habitat, flat shore walk.
child_note: Cameron Lakeshore Trail listed open (2026-10-12). Bear warning: GAP no specific warning listed for it.

name: Prince of Wales Hotel
what: Historic 1927 hotel on a bluff with a view of Upper Waterton Lake.
why_must_do: Classic photo; afternoon tea.
child_note: Prince of Wales Loop Trail open per 2026 page.

name: Upper and Lower Kananaskis Lakes
what: Two large glacial lakes with day-use areas, boat launch and short paved and gravel lakeside walks in Peter Lougheed Provincial Park.
why_must_do: Classic Kananaskis lake and Opal Range scenery with easy lakeside access for a child.
child_note: Lakeside strolls at Lower Lake and Interlakes are flat; keep away from shoreline in bear closure zones.

name: Elbow Falls
what: Waterfall viewpoint on the Elbow River reached by a short loop (0.8 km, about 27 m gain).
why_must_do: Easiest roadside waterfall near Calgary; pram-free short loop.
best_time: Any dry day; Hwy 66 closed Dec 1 - May 14, open in Sept
child_note: Fenced viewpoints; hold hands near rail.

name: Wedge Pond
what: 1 km flat loop around a pond under Mount Kidd, on Hwy 40 north of Kananaskis Village.
why_must_do: Reflection photo stop with no climbing.
child_note: Flat, 20-45 min.

name: Mount Lorette Ponds
what: Short loop (about 1 km) around small ponds near the Kananaskis River.
why_must_do: Quick easy picnic and pond stop for a young child.
child_note: Easy flat loop; check closure notices (day use appears in Alberta Parks closure notice).

name: Canmore Nordic Centre Provincial Park
what: GAP: summer use not verified (park has events pages on albertaparks.ca).
why_must_do: Base for Grassi Lakes access and trail network (INFERENCE).
child_note: GAP

name: Highwood Pass and Hwy 40 corridor
what: Hwy 40 pass area with trailheads for Ptarmigan Cirque and Pocaterra; road closed Dec 1 - Jun 14.
why_must_do: Gateway to larch cirque hiking; scenic drive.
best_time: Mid-Sept to early Oct for larches
child_note: Parking lot busy and construction reported; go early on weekdays.

name: Smith-Dorrien / Spray Trail (Hwy 742)
what: Unpaved scenic road between Canmore and Kananaskis Lakes giving access to Chester Lake, Burstall, Tent Ridge.
why_must_do: Access road for several Sept larch and family hikes.
child_note: Gravel, dusty, washboard, no cell service; GAP: Alberta Parks closure chart does not list it.

name: Mount Robson Visitor Centre viewpoint
what: Visitor centre back deck gives a clear view of Mount Robson (3,954 m, tallest in the Canadian Rockies).
why_must_do: Easiest look at the highest Rockies peak.
child_note: Zero walking; clouds often cover summit.

name: Overlander Falls
what: Waterfall on the Fraser River reached by a short walk of roughly 1.4 miles round trip near the visitor centre.
why_must_do: Short family walk in Robson Valley.
child_note: Easy for 6 year old; BC Parks lists it as a short family hike.

name: Kinney Lake
what: Turquoise lake about 7 km along the Berg Lake Trail; cycling permitted to Kinney Lake.
why_must_do: Most accessible lake on the Berg Lake trail.
child_note: Long but flat; 9-10 km return; see trail kinney-lake.

name: Berg Lake
what: Lake below Mount Robson reached by 23 km one-way trail; fully reopened June 2025 after 2021 flood repairs, reservations required May 27 - Sept 29 (2026 pattern).
why_must_do: Signature BC Rockies backpack; adult-only for this trip.
child_note: Not suitable for a 6 year old in a day; multi-day only with reservations.

name: Mount Assiniboine helicopter access
what: Helicopter flights from Mount Shark helipad run Wed, Fri and Sun; need a valid camping reservation to fly to the core area.
why_must_do: Only practical non-hiking access to Lake Magog.
child_note: GAP: child weight/fare and lodge pricing not found (Assiniboine Lodge site not fetched).

name: Lake Magog and Assiniboine core area
what: Core area with Magog Lake and Og Lake campgrounds; Sunburst Lake about 20 min walk away.
why_must_do: Matterhorn-style Mount Assiniboine view.
best_time: Early Sept for larches near Wonder Pass (INFERENCE)
child_note: Camping reservation via BC Parks; core sites sell out within seconds; huts via lodge.

name: Elk Lakes Provincial Park
what: Remote lakes reached by a roughly 67 km Forest Service Road; short flat trails (1 km to Lower Elk Lake).
why_must_do: Quiet alternative with easy lake walk.
child_note: Medium clearance vehicle, radio recommended; industrial traffic.

name: Beauvais Lake Provincial Park
what: Foothills lake park near Pincher Creek with Beauvais Lake Trail (about 6 miles) and Piney Point loop.
why_must_do: Info only for this trip; far south.
child_note: Listing marks main trail for older children.

name: Whiteswan Lake and Lussier Hot Springs
what: Free natural hot springs plus lake camping, via a logging road with heavy logging traffic.
why_must_do: Family friendly soak; swimsuit required, no dogs.
child_note: Steep path to springs; hot water 43 C - supervise child.

name: Castle Provincial Park
what: GAP: official park info not fetched; third-party lists Paradise Lake via Castle Mountain Resort as family-friendly.
why_must_do: Info only.
child_note: GAP

name: Top of the World Provincial Park
park: Top of the World Provincial Park
what: Remote park at the end of the Whiteswan logging road, trailhead at km 52.
why_must_do: Info only.
child_note: Remote; not for this trip.
